The Deva sletp in their hallowed halls, and elsewhere something awoke - the elder god Tymoro. He could see it in the lines of the planets and and in the warp and weft of existence - reality was coming to a close. A final grand overture before the ending note, an age of Oblivion. He hated to see it go, for it had been so young of a dimension, but he knew the irrevocable truth of the world - all things must end.

A decision he made - a decision to end reality with a lion's roar rather than the whimper of dying gods, of whom he would not be among. Mortality, mixed in a stew of fire and brimstone, a concoction of finality and fatalism that none could comprehend. In the beginning, a great blessing he had made, one of unity between the tiny particules in the great cosmic string. A blessing he would now snatch back as easily as it came.

It started on Gaea. Mar'dy, the bearer of the Amulet of Tymoro, felt a heat coming from his chest. Looking down, a bright flash and then… nothing. Oblivion. The Amulet had detonated, and with it vanished the binding of gravity on all existence. It propagated outwards, mortals being flung akimbo as their inertia threw them to hell. The atmosphere began to boil away, and then it was gone. Tectonic plates skittered off into the endess void, and moons went off to the heavens. The disappearance of gravity fled outwards like a bubble bursting, stars extinguishing as they boiled away and galaxys turning into nebulas and finally nothing.

And in the wreckage stood Tymoro, letting out a small *hmph*. He though to himself, *It was fun while it lasted.* A rift opened up, to where or what reality nobody knows, and he stepped through. It zipped up behind him, and he was never seen again.

As Tymoro unleashes his destruction, he feels a ... not a hand, but something on his shoulder.

Something is behind him, something beyond even his ability to properly perceive. Every time he has seen all of it he has seen but a 16th. It speaks, in a voice where every tone is itself a voice composed of infinite voices.

Not so fast. There is some time left yet, and you are leaving a mess. This world will end soon enough, in a more fitting fashion.

Turning towards his destruction, Tymoro sees it affect an atom, then travel half the distance to the next, then half of that, progressing continuously but without termination towards its destination.

It will reach its limiting behavior just after I have ensured all the destructors are functioning properly. I would prefer to avoid leaks, garbage collection is expensive.

With that the presence is gone. Tymoro is left to watch his destruction progressing endlessly, but without noticeable effect. Yet.
